# AWS SAM Reference & Patterns (Simplified)

This knowledge base provides essential AWS SAM templates, resource definitions, and policy patterns for the Serverless Migration project. This is a simplified version focusing on the most commonly used patterns.

## 1. Standard SAM Template Structure

### Header & Globals
```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31
Description: Serverless application infrastructure

Globals:
  Function:
    # Basic Configuration (Required)
    Runtime: python3.12  # Adjust based on actual code
    Handler: index.handler
    Timeout: 30  # seconds
    MemorySize: 512  # MB
    # Graviton: 20% lower GB-second price; as fast or faster in this project's
    # real-AWS A/B (m2s-mcp-server PERF_OPTIMIZATION_DESIGN.md A.4). Keep
    # x86_64 only when a dependency ships x86-only compiled modules.
    Architectures:
      - arm64
    
    # Environment Variables (Common)
    Environment:
      Variables:
        ENVIRONMENT: !Ref Environment
        LOG_LEVEL: INFO
    
    # Monitoring & Tracing (Recommended)
    Tracing: Active  # Enable X-Ray tracing
    
    # Shared Layers (Optional)
    Layers:
      - !Ref CommonLayer
    
    # Tags (Recommended)
    Tags:
      Project: MyProject
      Environment: !Ref Environment
```

### Parameters
```yaml
Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues: [dev, staging, prod]
```

## 2. Resource Patterns

### Lambda Function Pattern
```yaml
{LambdaName}Function:
  Type: AWS::Serverless::Function
  Properties:
    # ========== Required Configuration ==========
    CodeUri: backend/lambdas/{lambda_name}/
    Handler: handler.lambda_handler
    Runtime: python3.12  # python3.12, nodejs22.x, etc.
    
    # ========== Common Configuration ==========
    MemorySize: 512  # 128-10240 MB (affects CPU and cost)
    Timeout: 30  # seconds (max 900)
    
    Description: "Function description"  # Optional but recommended
    
    # Environment Variables
    Environment:
      Variables:
        TABLE_NAME: !Ref TableName

    # Shared Code Layers

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Transform: AWS::Serverless-2016-10-31
Description: >
  bookstore - shared infrastructure migrated from the Express monolith to
  API Gateway (REST) + Lambda + DynamoDB + SQS + Cognito. This part holds
  Globals / Parameters / every shared resource; the
  AWS::Serverless::Function resources and Outputs live in template.part2.yaml.
  Sources: storage/blueprint.json (metadata, api_gateway, cognito,
  dynamodb_tables, sqs_queues) and storage/analysis_report.json
  (global_middleware[0], dynamodb_info.table_schemas).

Parameters:
  Environment:
    Type: String
    Default: dev
    AllowedValues:
      - dev
      - staging
      - prod
    Description: Stage / name prefix for every resource this stack creates.

Globals:
  Function:
    # No Handler here on purpose: the blueprint's "handler.handler" is the
    # architect's placeholder, the real file/export names come from
    # output/lambdas/ and are written per function in part2. Policies,
    # Environment.Variables and Events are per function too (part2).
    Runtime: nodejs22.x          # blueprint lambda_functions[].runtime (D-2)
    Timeout: 30                  # consumer stays at 30s < queue VisibilityTimeout 300s (D-3)
    MemorySize: 512
    # No "Tracing: Active": api_gateway.api_type_reason records that the
    # application uses no X-Ray, and active tracing is not a behaviour the
    # migration has to keep (it only adds span cost). Same reason there is no
    # TracingEnabled on the Api below.
    # Graviton: lower GB-second price, at least as fast (m2s-sam-kb Header &
    # Globals; PERF_OPTIMIZATION.md B1). No x86-only compiled module here:
    # the functions depend on @aws-sdk/* clients only.
    Architectures:
      - arm64

Resources:
  # ==========================================================================
  # API Gateway - REST (blueprint api_gateway.api_type = "rest")
  # ==========================================================================
  # Why REST (api_gateway.api_type_reason / D-9): the app-wide cors middleware
  # (analysis_report global_middleware[0], server.js:29-32) puts
  # Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true on EVERY response next to
  # Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, and the responses API Gateway generates
  # itself (authorizer 401, undefined route 4xx, integration 5xx) need
  # GatewayResponses to carry them - only REST has that.
  # No TracingEnabled: api_gateway.api_type_reason records that this
  # application uses no X-Ray (and no WAF / API keys / request validation /
  # stage caching / resource policy).
  BookstoreApi:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::Api
    Properties:
      # api_gateway.integration: every path is a Lambda proxy integration
      # (AWS_PROXY), which is what a SAM Api event without RequestParameters
      # produces - so handlers keep the REST event shape the spec records
      # (event.requestContext.authorizer.claims, pathParameters,
      # queryStringParameters AND multiValueQueryStringParameters, headers,
      # body), including the "?q=a&q=b -> array -> 500" arm of
      # GET /api/search (api_gateway.notes, D-11).
      # api_gateway.throttling: no MethodSettings / per-stage limits - the
      # monolith cannot answer 429, so adding them would invent a response.
      StageName: !Ref Environment
      # api_gateway.endpoint_configuration: clients = same_region (AT2).
      EndpointConfiguration:
        Type: REGIONAL
      # api_gateway.cors. These strings only drive the generated preflight
      # OPTIONS methods (they are not applied to real responses), and the
      # preflight stays unauthorized - api_gateway.cors.note "预检不挂授权器",
      # which is what global_middleware[0].note records for the monolith: cors
      # answers OPTIONS in place (204, no next()), so neither the routes nor
      # authMiddleware ever see a preflight. The real responses get their
      # headers from the functions (D-9 第 1 条) and from GatewayResponses below.
      Cors:
        AllowMethods: "'GET,POST,PUT,DELETE,OPTIONS'"
        AllowHeaders: "'Authorization,Content-Type,Access-Control-Request-Headers'"
        AllowOrigin: "'*'"
      # Access logs (m2s-sam-kb ApiLogGroup companion; PERF_OPTIMIZATION.md B4).
      # The format is the one this pipeline's own AWS E2E harness deploys and
      # parses: responseLatency minus integrationLatency is the time API Gateway
      # itself spent (including the Cognito authorizer), which is what an E2E
      # measurement needs to split "gateway" from "Lambda".
      AccessLogSetting:
        DestinationArn: !GetAtt ApiLogGroup.Arn
        Format: '$context.requestId $context.status $context.responseLatency $context.integrationLatency'
      # api_gateway.authorizer = Cognito, authorizer_type = COGNITO_USER_POOLS
      # (D-1). Every auth="required" event inherits DefaultAuthorizer, so part2
      # must NOT add an Auth block on those events. Identity source is the
      # Authorization header, token validation is done by the gateway layer
      # (api_gateway.token_validation); no scopes are configured
      # (api_gateway.auth_scopes) because the monolith only checked signature+exp.
      Auth:
        DefaultAuthorizer: CognitoAuthorizer
        Authorizers:
          CognitoAuthorizer:
            UserPoolArn: !GetAtt CognitoUserPool.Arn

      # GatewayResponses (api_gateway.gateway_responses; gate GM2, D-9 第 2/3 条)
      # Every header recorded in analysis_report global_middleware[0] has to be
      # present on the gateway's own 4xx/5xx: API Gateway answers those without
      # ever calling a Lambda, so the cors middleware's headers cannot reach
      # them any other way. Values are single-quoted strings (SAM writes them
      # as method.response.header.* literals).
      #   * Access-Control-Allow-Origin / -Credentials: what the monolith sends
      #     on every non-OPTIONS response (server.js:30-31).
      #   * Content-Type: the gateway's own JSON error body
      #     {"message": <网关文案>}; the body text differs from the monolith's
      #     {error: ...} and that difference is ruled in advance by R-A1-a3-1
      #     (status 401 itself is kept).

      #     four remaining global_middleware[0] names. The monolith emitted
      #     them only on the preflight cors answered itself (2.8.5 defaults,
      #     204 + Content-Length: 0), so a function must never put them on a
      #     real response (D-9 第 3 条) - and cannot get them there by accident
      #     either, because GatewayResponses only rewrites responses API
      #     Gateway generates itself. GM2 checks that every app-wide header
      #     name is present on DEFAULT_4XX / DEFAULT_5XX; the literals below

#     name is present on DEFAULT_4XX / DEFAULT_5XX; the literals below

      #     the real Content-Length of the body it renders.
      # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

        DEFAULT_4XX:
          ResponseParameters:
            Headers:
              Access-Control-Allow-Origin: "'*'"
              Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: "'true'"
              Content-Type: "'application/json'"
              Access-Control-Allow-Methods: "'GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE'"
              Access-Control-Allow-Headers: "'Authorization,Content-Type,Access-Control-Request-Headers'"
              Vary: "'Access-Control-Request-Headers'"
              Content-Length: "'0'"

          ResponseParameters:
            Headers:
              Access-Control-Allow-Origin: "'*'"
              Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: "'true'"
              Content-Type: "'application/json'"
              Access-Control-Allow-Methods: "'GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE'"
              Access-Control-Allow-Headers: "'Authorization,Content-Type,Access-Control-Request-Headers'"
              Vary: "'Access-Control-Request-Headers'"
              Content-Length: "'0'"

  # Cognito User Pool (blueprint cognito.enabled = true; D-1 / D-4 / R-A1-a3-3)
  # ==========================================================================
  # The four /api/auth/* endpoints and the whole Bookstore-Users table are
  # replaced by this pool: clients call the Cognito SDK directly, so there is
  # no auth Lambda and no user table in DynamoDB. No LambdaConfig / trigger
  # function is configured (cognito.no_cognito_triggers).
  CognitoUserPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPool
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      UserPoolName: !Sub ${Environment}-bookstore-users
      # cognito.user_pool_attributes = [email, name] are both standard
      # Cognito attributes, so Schema stays empty: Schema is ONLY for custom
      # attributes. email is the sign-in attribute and is auto-verified
      # (the monolith's register took email as the login name).
      UsernameAttributes:
        - email
      AutoVerifiedAttributes:
        - email
      Policies:
        PasswordPolicy:
          # cognito.password_policy: the only strength check the monolith ever
          # proved was routes/auth.js:40 (password.length < 6); Cognito needs
          # at least one character class, so RequireNumbers carries the rest
          # (D-1, noted as a rulebook default, not a choice). All five fields
          # are written explicitly so the deployed policy is the blueprint's
          # (gate C14).
          MinimumLength: 6
          RequireNumbers: true
          RequireSymbols: false
          RequireUppercase: false
          RequireLowercase: false

    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient

Value: !Ref Environment

  IdempotencyTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    DeletionPolicy: Retain
    UpdateReplacePolicy: Retain
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub ${Environment}-bookstore-idempotency
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: pk
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: pk
          KeyType: HASH
      # dynamodb_tables[4]: target-only dedupe table for the SQS consumer

  # ==========================================================================
  # SQS (blueprint sqs_queues[0] = BestsellerUpdateQueue; D-3)
  # ==========================================================================
  # POST /api/orders' fire-and-forget bestseller update becomes a message:
  # producer orders-create, single consumer update-bestsellers. The HTTP
  # contract stays independent of this queue (SI-8: a failed, delayed or
  # retried update never changes the order response).
  BestsellerUpdateQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      QueueName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-bestseller-update-queue'
      # sqs_queues[0].visibility_timeout = 300s, far above the consumer's 30s
      # timeout, so one message is not handed to a second batch while it is
      # still being processed.
      VisibilityTimeout: 300
      RedrivePolicy:
        deadLetterTargetArn: !GetAtt BestsellerUpdateQueueDLQ.Arn
        # sqs_queues[0].max_receive_count = 3: after three failed receives the
        # message goes to the DLQ instead of spinning forever.
        maxReceiveCount: 3

    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    Properties:
      QueueName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-bestseller-update-queue-dlq'

  # reuses: response()/errorResponse()/fromException() carry
  # global_middleware[0]'s headers, parseBody() the bodyParser 100kb / 400 / 413

  # Layer", gate C13): with Metadata.BuildMethod sam build puts its contents
  # under nodejs/ at runtime, i.e. /opt/nodejs/shared.js - which is what the
  # handlers require('/opt/nodejs/shared') resolves to.
  SharedLayer:
    Type: AWS::Serverless::LayerVersion
    Properties:
      ContentUri: layers/shared/nodejs/
      CompatibleRuntimes:
        - nodejs22.x
    Metadata:
      BuildMethod: nodejs22.x

  # Lambda functions (blueprint lambda_functions: 12 entries, all nodejs22.x)
  # ==========================================================================
  # This block is the second half of Resources: m2s-mcp-server/m2s_merge.py
  # concatenates it right after template.part1.yaml (which ends with its shared
  # resources metadata block), so everything below stays indented under
  # `Resources:` and the file ends with Outputs at column 0. The only metadata
  # marker pair in this file is the FUNCTIONS_METADATA one further down.
  #
  # What is taken from where:
  #   * CodeUri / Handler  - the real directories and export names on disk
  #     (output/lambdas/bookstore/<name>/handler.js, each ending in
  #     `exports.handler = ...`). blueprint.lambda_functions[].handler is the
  #     architect's placeholder ("handler.handler"); it happens to equal the
  #     real value here, and it is verified against the files, not copied
  #     from the blueprint (gate C3).
  #     CodeUri is relative to output/ and ends with "/" (gates C1/C2).
  #   * Runtime/Timeout/MemorySize/Architectures - inherited from
  #     Globals.Function in part1; blueprint gives no per-function timeout or
  #     memory (all null), and D-3 needs the consumer to stay under the
  #     queue's VisibilityTimeout 300s, which the shared 30s already does.
  #   * Environment.Variables - exactly blueprint
  #     lambda_functions[].environment_variables, nothing added: D-39 says the
  #     table/queue names come only from each function's own variables (the
  #     monolith's utils/dynamodb.js defaults are not migrated), and the gate's
  #     env prescreen treats a declared-but-unused variable as a finding.
  #     "${BooksTable}" in the blueprint means "the BooksTable resource", i.e.
  #     !Ref BooksTable (part1's dynamodb_table_logical_names).
  #   * Policies - SAM policy templates only (m2s-sam-kb "Policy Decision
  #     Tree": DynamoDB -> DynamoDBCrudPolicy, SQS send -> SQSSendMessagePolicy,
  #     SQS consume -> SQSPollerPolicy), one per table/queue the handler itself
  #     touches; no catch-all role, no inline statements.
  #   * Events - blueprint lambda_functions[].entry_points / trigger_type.
  #     api_gateway.api_type = "rest" (AT2): every HTTP event is `Type: Api`

  #     shape the spec records (event.requestContext.authorizer.claims,
  #     pathParameters, queryStringParameters AND

  #   * Layers - the 11 API handlers all start with

    checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    suspects: dict[str, Any] = {}
    severe = False

    if phase == "blueprint":
        checks = check_b0(ws) + check_contract(ws) + check_dm(ws) + check_api_type(ws)
